newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister's stepdaughter in fraud case.
newsitem.headline: French minister's stepdaughter in fraud case.

text.p: The stepdaughter of French Justice Minister Jacques Toubon, Sophie Deniau, was placed under judicial investigation on Wednesday on suspicion of business fraud and barred from leaving the country, justice sources said.
The allegations stem from Deniau's role in the financial affairs of the Isola-2000 ski station in the French Alps, which is now in serious financial difficulty, the sources said.
She was released on 750,000 francs ($150,000) bail on condition that she refrain from meeting others involved in the case or from running a commercial company.
Deniau, daughter of Toubon's wife Lise by a previous marriage, is in her early 30s and married to the son of former centrist cabinet minister Jean-Francois Deniau.
Two other people were also placed under investigation, one of them businessman Dominique Bouillon, who was remanded in custody pending a possible trial.

The case was launched by a complaint from the Societe de Banque Occidentale, a former subsidiary of the Credit Lyonnais bank, which lent Bouillon and his associates 100 million francs ($20 million) to buy Isola-2000 in 1991, the sources said.
